itemListElement.name: Granola AI Pricing in 2026: What US Users Actually Pay

mainEntity.name: How much is Granola per month?

acceptedAnswer.text: Business costs $14 per user per month and Enterprise costs $35 per user per month. The Basic plan is free. For a 10-person team, that comes to $1,680 a year on Business and $4,200 on Enterprise. Students and accepted startups can get 12 months of Business free, and nonprofits get 50% off.

Yes. Granola Basic is free with no time limit, but it keeps only 30 days of meeting history. To keep older notes, you need Business at $14 per user per month. Notes older than 30 days are stored, not deleted, but you cannot open them until you upgrade. Export titles and summaries as a CSV before relying on Basic alone.

Only on Enterprise. Granola's help center says Basic and Business are billed monthly and annual billing is available on Enterprise contracts only. Business is billed per user each month, so you can add or remove seats as your team changes without a yearly commitment.

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between Granola Business and Enterprise?

acceptedAnswer.text: Business ($14) adds unlimited history, advanced AI models and integrations. Enterprise ($35) adds SSO, admin controls, org-wide auto-deletion, usage analytics and priority support. Most teams under 50 people only need Business unless their security review requires single sign-on, which is the main reason to pay $35.

mainEntity.name: Does Granola charge per meeting or per minute?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Billing is per user per month, and none of the plans list a minute or meeting cap; on the free plan the limit is 30 days of history. Heavy users get predictable costs as a result. Long meetings and many meetings cost the same as light use on the same plan.

mainEntity.name: Is there a cheaper alternative to Granola?

acceptedAnswer.text: Fireflies Pro costs $10 per seat billed yearly and Fathom's free plan records unlimited calls. Lynkk costs $15 a month and adds prep, live answers and Jira tickets. Which option is cheapest depends on your bottleneck.
